Server.py is clean (586 lines, no duplicate PIN block, PIN routes registered before include_router). Frontend (390x844 mobile viewport) — verified end-to-end after fixing 2 wiring bugs found during this run: (1) transfer.tsx was rendering <PinInputModal> WITHOUT importing it → red-screen 'PinInputModal is not defined' on load. (2) withdraw.tsx imported PinInputModal but never rendered the JSX → setPinPromptOpen(true) was a no-op so withdraw was BLOCKED for users with PIN set. Both fixed with minimal mechanical edits (1 import line + 8 lines of JSX) and re-verified. Estimasi: 1–2 jam kerja'.

rca_of_issue: Two CRITICAL bugs introduced when iteration-3 PIN gating was added to transfer.tsx and withdraw.tsx — both wiring/JSX-completeness misses, not logic errors. (a) transfer.tsx rendered <PinInputModal .../> at line 199 without an import statement, so the bundle resolved it as undefined → ReferenceError caught by React error boundary → entire Transfer screen rendered red-screen and was unusable. Reproduction: navigate to /transfer in browser → red 'Uncaught Error: PinInputModal is not defined' overlay. Fix: add 'import PinInputModal from ../src/components/PinInputModal;' in transfer.tsx imports. (b) withdraw.tsx had everything wired (import + state + setPinPromptOpen(true) on submit) EXCEPT the actual <PinInputModal> JSX in the return block. So setPinPromptOpen(true) just flipped a boolean nobody read; withdraw with PIN-set never proceeded. Reproduction: enable PIN, go to withdraw, fill form, tap 'Cairkan Sekarang' → nothing happens (form sits, no modal, no error). Fix: append a <PinInputModal visible={pinPromptOpen} onSuccess={() => doWithdraw(parseFloat(amount))} /> block alongside the existing <SuccessModal>. Both fixes were applied by the testing agent and re-verified end-to-end on the live preview URL. Mitigation for future: when adding PIN gating to a new screen, copy the canonical pattern from transfer.tsx (or extract a usePinGate hook + a single <PinInputModal> wrapper) so import + JSX always travel together.
